summary:
Sud is a region of Italy and stands under the Italian national framework. No regional statute, court ruling or administrative measure addressing gender identity or sexual orientation was identified, so the assessment for the region rests on documented incidents.

ILGA-Europe's country review for Italy, published in February 2025, records a bias-motivated assault in Scampia, in the Naples area, in which a young man was attacked by assailants riding a scooter.

On 13 October 2025 a 63-year-old man was arrested in Torre Annunziata, in the province of Naples, after making stabbing threats against a young LGBTQIA+ activist. Local reporting treated the episode as a grave homophobic attack in the Naples area.

Both documented episodes occurred in the Naples metropolitan area. Neither is recorded as directed at a visitor, and no comparable incident is documented elsewhere in Sud, so the anti-LGBTQ violence recorded in the region is concentrated in that conurbation.
tangentialFactors:
Both documented episodes in Sud fall in the Naples metropolitan area, and the victims are recorded as a young man and a local activist rather than as visitors. The concentration reflects where incidents were reported, not a measured distribution of risk across the region.

Neither episode is recorded as a trans-specific attack, and neither source identifies the victims as transgender; the region's documented violence is recorded against the wider LGBTI population of the Naples area.
localsOnly:
Transgender residents of Sud have no regional anti-discrimination instrument or dedicated support body documented in the sources reviewed; the protections that apply are set at national level.

Both documented episodes involved local people rather than visitors, a young man in Scampia and an activist in Torre Annunziata. Trans residents in the Naples area face the same street-level risk documented for the wider LGBTI population there.

No health, shelter or support service for transgender residents specific to Sud is documented.
outOfScopeNotes:
The ILGA-Europe review is dated February 2025 but is cited for an assault in Scampia placed in March 2025; the discrepancy is unresolved in the source.

No custodial facility, unit or policy for transgender detainees specific to Sud is documented; arrangements for trans prisoners are set at national level and are not region-specific.

No statement by a regional or municipal authority in Sud on either documented episode was identified, and no regional enforcement data on anti-LGBT violence is published.
